meta.topic: 存在唯一性、延拓、连续依赖、比较定理、稳定性与 Lyapunov 方法

zh: 考虑初值问题 $y'=f(x,y)$、$y(x_0)=y_0$。若 $y$ 是 $C^1$ 解，则在 $[x_0,x]$ 上积分得 $$y(x)=y_0+\int_{x_0}^{x}f(t,y(t))\,dt.$$ 反之，若 $y$ 连续且满足此积分方程，则右端可微（$f$ 连续、$y$ 连续），求导得 $y'=f(x,y)$，且 $y(x_0)=y_0$。因此 $C^1$ 解与连续函数空间中的积分方程不动点一一对应。

设 $f$ 在矩形 $$R=\{(x,y):|x-x_0|\le a,\ |y-y_0|\le b\}$$ 上连续，其中 $a>0,b>0$，且关于 $y$ 满足 Lipschitz 条件 $$|f(x,y_1)-f(x,y_2)|\le L|y_1-y_2|.$$ 令 $M=\max_R|f|$。$M=0$ 时 $y\equiv y_0$ 是解；$L=0$ 时 $f$ 与 $y$ 无关，结论直接由积分得到。以下设 $M>0$、$L>0$，取 $$h=\min\left\{a,\frac{b}{M},\frac{1}{2L}\right\}.$$ 这些常数保证 Picard 迭代不逃出矩形，并且是压缩的。

在 $C([x_0-h,x_0+h])$ 上定义 Picard 算子 $$(Ty)(x)=y_0+\int_{x_0}^{x}f(t,y(t))\,dt,$$ 并取 sup 范数 $\|y\|_\infty=\max_{|x-x_0|\le h}|y(x)|$。若 $\|y-y_0\|_\infty\le b$，则 $$|(Ty)(x)-y_0|\le\int_{x_0}^{x}|f(t,y(t))|\,dt\le M|x-x_0|\le Mh\le b,$$ 故 $T$ 把闭球 $\overline B(y_0,b)$ 映入自身。

对闭球内任意 $y,z$，由 Lipschitz 条件 $$\begin{aligned}|(Ty)(x)-(Tz)(x)|&\le\int_{x_0}^{x}|f(t,y(t))-f(t,z(t))|\,dt\\&\le L|x-x_0|\,\|y-z\|_\infty\le Lh\|y-z\|_\infty.\end{aligned}$$ 取 $h\le1/(2L)$ 得压缩因子 $q=Lh\le1/2<1$，所以 $T$ 是压缩映射。

闭球 $\overline B(y_0,b)$ 在 sup 范数下完备，由 Banach 压缩映射原理，$T$ 有唯一不动点 $y^*$。它满足积分方程，从而是 $C^1$ 解；并且任意解在 $|x-x_0|\le h$ 上都满足 $|y(x)-y_0|\le Mh\le b$，必是该闭球中的不动点，故解唯一。Picard 迭代 $y_{n+1}=Ty_n$ 以几何速度收敛到 $y^*$。结论是局部的：只保证在 $|x-x_0|\le h$ 上存在唯一。

条件不能减弱为「$f$ 连续」：Peano 定理只由连续性给出至少一个局部解，不保证唯一。反例 $y'=\sqrt{|y|}$、$y(0)=0$ 中 $f$ 连续，但在 $y=0$ 处 $$\frac{|f(y)-f(0)|}{|y|}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{|y|}}\to+\infty,$$ 不满足 Lipschitz 条件；$y\equiv0$ 与 $y=(x-c)^2/4$（$x\ge c$，左侧接 $0$，$c\ge0$）都是过原点的解，故唯一性失效。若 $\partial f/\partial y$ 在 $R$ 上连续，则由中值定理 $f$ 关于 $y$ 满足 Lipschitz 条件，这是最常用的充分判据。
en: Consider the initial value problem $y'=f(x,y)$, $y(x_0)=y_0$. If $y$ is a $C^1$ solution, integrating over $[x_0,x]$ gives $$y(x)=y_0+\int_{x_0}^{x}f(t,y(t))\,dt.$$ Conversely, if $y$ is continuous and satisfies this integral equation, the right-hand side is differentiable (because $f$ and $y$ are continuous); differentiating gives $y'=f(x,y)$ and $y(x_0)=y_0$. Thus $C^1$ solutions correspond exactly to fixed points of this integral equation in the space of continuous functions.

Assume $f$ is continuous on the rectangle $$R=\{(x,y):|x-x_0|\le a,\ |y-y_0|\le b\}$$ with $a>0,b>0$, and satisfies the Lipschitz condition in $y$: $$|f(x,y_1)-f(x,y_2)|\le L|y_1-y_2|.$$ Let $M=\max_R|f|$. If $M=0$, then $y\equiv y_0$ is a solution; if $L=0$, then $f$ is independent of $y$ and the conclusion follows directly by integration. Henceforth assume $M>0$ and $L>0$, and set $$h=\min\left\{a,\frac{b}{M},\frac{1}{2L}\right\}.$$ These constants keep the Picard iterates inside the rectangle and make the map a contraction.

On $C([x_0-h,x_0+h])$ define the Picard operator $$(Ty)(x)=y_0+\int_{x_0}^{x}f(t,y(t))\,dt$$ and use the sup norm $\|y\|_\infty=\max_{|x-x_0|\le h}|y(x)|$. If $\|y-y_0\|_\infty\le b$, then $$|(Ty)(x)-y_0|\le\int_{x_0}^{x}|f(t,y(t))|\,dt\le M|x-x_0|\le Mh\le b,$$ so $T$ maps the closed ball $\overline B(y_0,b)$ into itself.

For any $y,z$ in the closed ball, the Lipschitz condition gives $$\begin{aligned}|(Ty)(x)-(Tz)(x)|&\le\int_{x_0}^{x}|f(t,y(t))-f(t,z(t))|\,dt\\&\le L|x-x_0|\,\|y-z\|_\infty\le Lh\|y-z\|_\infty.\end{aligned}$$ Since $h\le1/(2L)$, the contraction factor is $q=Lh\le1/2<1$, so $T$ is a contraction.

The closed ball $\overline B(y_0,b)$ is complete in the sup norm, so by the Banach fixed point theorem $T$ has a unique fixed point $y^*$. It satisfies the integral equation and hence is a $C^1$ solution. Moreover, any solution on $|x-x_0|\le h$ satisfies $|y(x)-y_0|\le Mh\le b$, so it lies in the closed ball and must be that fixed point; uniqueness follows. The Picard iterates $y_{n+1}=Ty_n$ converge geometrically to $y^*$. The conclusion is local: existence and uniqueness are guaranteed only on $|x-x_0|\le h$.

The hypothesis cannot be weakened to continuity of $f$: Peano's theorem yields at least one local solution from continuity alone, but not uniqueness. In $y'=\sqrt{|y|}$, $y(0)=0$, the function $f$ is continuous, yet at $y=0$ $$\frac{|f(y)-f(0)|}{|y|}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{|y|}}\to+\infty,$$ so no Lipschitz constant exists. Both $y\equiv0$ and $y=(x-c)^2/4$ (for $x\ge c$, joined to $0$ on the left, $c\ge0$) are solutions through the origin, so uniqueness fails. If $\partial f/\partial y$ is continuous on $R$, the mean value theorem makes $f$ Lipschitz in $y$; this is the usual sufficient test.

zh: 设 $f(t,y)$ 在包含两条轨线的紧集上连续、关于 $y$ 局部 Lipschitz。固定有限 $T>t_0$，设 $y(t)=y(t;y_0)$ 与 $z(t)=y(t;z_0)$ 都在 $[t_0,T]$ 上有定义。连续依赖是指：对任意 $\varepsilon>0$ 存在 $\delta>0$，只要 $|y_0-z_0|<\delta$，就有 $$\sup_{t\in[t_0,T]}|y(t)-z(t)|<\varepsilon.$$ 这里 $\delta$ 可以依赖参考初值 $y_0$、$\varepsilon$ 和 $T$，但不能依赖扰动后的 $z_0$；若要求在一个初值集合上一致，则需额外的一致 Lipschitz 或有界性条件。结论是有限时间区间上的一致估计。

由积分方程，$$\begin{aligned}y(t)-z(t)&=(y_0-z_0)\\&\quad+\int_{t_0}^{t}\bigl[f(s,y(s))-f(s,z(s))\bigr]ds.\end{aligned}$$ 令 $u(t)=|y(t)-z(t)|$。两条轨线落在同一紧集内，局部 Lipschitz 条件给出统一常数 $L$，于是 $$u(t)\le|y_0-z_0|+L\int_{t_0}^{t}u(s)\,ds,\qquad t_0\le t\le T.$$
对 $u$ 用 Gronwall 引理：取 $\beta(s)\equiv L\ge0$、$\alpha=|y_0-z_0|$，得 $$u(t)\le|y_0-z_0|\,e^{L(t-t_0)}\le|y_0-z_0|\,e^{L(T-t_0)}.$$ 证明只用到 $u$ 连续与 $L\ge0$；$L=0$ 时结论退化为 $u(t)\le|y_0-z_0|$。

因此给定 $\varepsilon>0$，取 $\delta=\varepsilon e^{-L(T-t_0)}$：当 $|y_0-z_0|<\delta$ 时，对一切 $t\in[t_0,T]$ 有 $|y(t)-z(t)|<\varepsilon$。这证明了连续依赖；与存在性、唯一性合起来，初值问题在 Hadamard 意义下适定。指数因子 $e^{L(T-t_0)}$ 说明误差最多被放大这么多倍：$L$ 大或区间长时数值预测会迅速变差，但在有限区间上依赖仍是连续的。

对含参数问题 $y'=f(t,y,\lambda)$，设 $f$ 在紧邻域内连续且关于 $(y,\lambda)$ Lipschitz，常数为 $L_y,L_\lambda$。设两解的初值分别为 $y_0,z_0$、参数分别为 $\lambda_1,\lambda_2$，对应的解为 $y(t),z(t)$，则 $$\begin{aligned}u(t)&\le|y_0-z_0|+L_\lambda|\lambda_1-\lambda_2|(T-t_0)\\&\quad+L_y\int_{t_0}^{t}u(s)\,ds.\end{aligned}$$ Gronwall 给出 $$\begin{aligned}\sup_{[t_0,T]}u&\le\Bigl(|y_0-z_0|+L_\lambda|\lambda_1-\lambda_2|(T-t_0)\Bigr)\\&\quad\times e^{L_y(T-t_0)},\end{aligned}$$ 所以解对初值和参数都连续依赖，参数扰动被同一个指数因子放大。

若进一步 $f$ 关于 $y$（以及参数 $\lambda$）连续可微，则解对初值、参数也连续可微（对参数求导时固定初值；对初值求导时初值本身是变量）。形式推导：记 $v=\partial y/\partial y_0$，对积分方程求导得 $$v(t)=1+\int_{t_0}^{t}f_y(s,y(s))v(s)\,ds,$$ 即 $$v'=f_y(t,y(t))v,\qquad v(t_0)=1.$$ 对参数记 $w=\partial y/\partial\lambda$，则 $$w'=f_y(t,y(t))w+f_\lambda(t,y(t),\lambda),\qquad w(t_0)=0.$$ 这两条第一变分方程都是线性方程，其解给出灵敏度；可微性通常要求 $f$ 关于 $y$ 连续可微；仅有 Lipschitz 不足以保证。
en: Let $f(t,y)$ be continuous on a compact set containing both trajectories and locally Lipschitz in $y$. Fix a finite $T>t_0$ and suppose $y(t)=y(t;y_0)$ and $z(t)=y(t;z_0)$ are both defined on $[t_0,T]$. Continuous dependence means: for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ such that $|y_0-z_0|<\delta$ implies $$\sup_{t\in[t_0,T]}|y(t)-z(t)|<\varepsilon.$$ Here $\delta$ may depend on the reference initial value $y_0$, on $\varepsilon$ and on $T$, but not on the perturbed value $z_0$; a uniform statement over a whole set of initial values requires an additional uniform Lipschitz or boundedness condition. The estimate is uniform on a finite time interval.

The integral equations give $$\begin{aligned}y(t)-z(t)&=(y_0-z_0)\\&\quad+\int_{t_0}^{t}\bigl[f(s,y(s))-f(s,z(s))\bigr]ds.\end{aligned}$$ Set $u(t)=|y(t)-z(t)|$. Both trajectories lie in one compact set, so the local Lipschitz condition supplies a uniform constant $L$, and $$u(t)\le|y_0-z_0|+L\int_{t_0}^{t}u(s)\,ds,\qquad t_0\le t\le T.$$

Apply Gronwall's lemma to $u$ with $\beta(s)\equiv L\ge0$ and $\alpha=|y_0-z_0|$: $$u(t)\le|y_0-z_0|\,e^{L(t-t_0)}\le|y_0-z_0|\,e^{L(T-t_0)}.$$ Only continuity of $u$ and $L\ge0$ are used; when $L=0$ this reduces to $u(t)\le|y_0-z_0|$.

Thus, given $\varepsilon>0$, take $\delta=\varepsilon e^{-L(T-t_0)}$: if $|y_0-z_0|<\delta$, then $|y(t)-z(t)|<\varepsilon$ for every $t\in[t_0,T]$. This proves continuous dependence; together with existence and uniqueness it makes the initial value problem well posed in Hadamard's sense. The factor $e^{L(T-t_0)}$ is the maximal amplification of the error: large $L$ or a long interval degrades numerical prediction rapidly, but dependence remains continuous on every finite interval.

For a parameter-dependent problem $y'=f(t,y,\lambda)$, assume $f$ is continuous on a compact neighborhood and Lipschitz in $(y,\lambda)$ with constants $L_y,L_\lambda$. Let the two solutions have initial values $y_0,z_0$ and parameters $\lambda_1,\lambda_2$, and denote them by $y(t),z(t)$. Then $$\begin{aligned}u(t)&\le|y_0-z_0|+L_\lambda|\lambda_1-\lambda_2|(T-t_0)\\&\quad+L_y\int_{t_0}^{t}u(s)\,ds.\end{aligned}$$ Gronwall gives $$\begin{aligned}\sup_{[t_0,T]}u&\le\Bigl(|y_0-z_0|+L_\lambda|\lambda_1-\lambda_2|(T-t_0)\Bigr)\\&\quad\times e^{L_y(T-t_0)},\end{aligned}$$ so the solution depends continuously on both the initial value and the parameter, with the same exponential amplification.

If in addition $f$ is continuously differentiable in $y$ (and in the parameter $\lambda$), then the solution is continuously differentiable in the initial value and the parameter (for differentiation in the parameter the initial value is fixed; for differentiation in the initial value, the initial value itself is the variable). Formally, let $v=\partial y/\partial y_0$; differentiating the integral equation gives $$v(t)=1+\int_{t_0}^{t}f_y(s,y(s))v(s)\,ds,$$ that is, $$v'=f_y(t,y(t))v,\qquad v(t_0)=1.$$ For the parameter, let $w=\partial y/\partial\lambda$; then $$w'=f_y(t,y(t))w+f_\lambda(t,y(t),\lambda),\qquad w(t_0)=0.$$ These first variation equations are linear and yield the sensitivities. Differentiability typically requires $f$ to be continuously differentiable in $y$; Lipschitz continuity alone is not enough.

zh: 设 $f$ 在开集 $D\subset\mathbb R^2$ 上连续且关于 $y$ 局部 Lipschitz，$(t_0,y_0)\in D$。Picard–Lindelöf 定理给出过 $(t_0,y_0)$ 的局部解。若两个解分别在含 $t_0$ 的开区间 $I_1,I_2$ 上有定义，则由唯一性它们在 $I_1\cap I_2$ 上相等，于是可拼接成 $I_1\cup I_2$ 上的解。把所有这样的区间取并，得到最大存在区间 $(a,b)$；它含 $t_0$，且解在 $(a,b)$ 上由初值唯一确定。
最大区间必为开区间。若 $b<+\infty$ 且解在 $t\to b^-$ 时有有限极限 $y_*$、$(b,y_*)\in D$，则在 $(b,y_*)$ 处再次应用局部存在唯一性定理，可把解延拓到 $b$ 的右侧，矛盾。因此要么 $b=+\infty$，要么 $t\to b^-$ 时 $(t,y(t))$ 不留在 $D$ 的任何紧子集内；左端点 $a$ 同理。
这就是爆炸性替代：当 $b<+\infty$ 时，对 $D$ 的每个紧子集 $K$，都存在 $t_K<b$，使当 $t_K<t<b$ 时 $(t,y(t))\notin K$。特别地，若 $D=\mathbb R^2$，则必有 $|y(t)|\to+\infty$；若 $D$ 有边界，则其聚点只能落在 $\partial D$ 上或趋于无穷。解不会在 $D$ 内部以有限值「平静地」停止。

例：$y'=y^2$、$y(0)=1$。分离变量得 $-1/y=t+C$，由初值得 $$y(t)=\frac{1}{1-t},\qquad t\in(-\infty,1).$$ 当 $t\to1^-$ 时 $y\to+\infty$，故解不能在 $t=1$ 之后延拓，最大存在区间是 $(-\infty,1)$。一般地，$y(0)=a>0$ 时 $y=a/(1-at)$，爆破时刻 $T_*=1/a$。

线性方程在系数连续区间的内部不会发生有限时间爆破；但端点 $\alpha,\beta$ 处 $p,q$ 本身可能无界，所以不能断言解在端点有有限极限。设最大右端点为 $b$ 且 $b<\beta$。因为 $[t_0,b]\subset(\alpha,\beta)$ 是紧区间，$P=\max_{[t_0,b]}|p|$、$Q=\max_{[t_0,b]}|q|$ 有限。对 $t\in[t_0,b)$，积分方程与 Gronwall 给出 $$|y(t)|\le\bigl(|y_0|+Q(b-t_0)\bigr)e^{P(b-t_0)}.$$ 又 $|y'|\le P|y|+Q$ 也有界，故 $y$ 在 $[t_0,b)$ 上一致连续，极限 $y_*=\lim_{t\to b^-}y(t)$ 存在且 $(b,y_*)\in(\alpha,\beta)\times\mathbb R^n$。由局部存在唯一性，解可从 $(b,y_*)$ 继续向右延拓，这与 $b$ 是最大右端点矛盾。因此 $b=\beta$；同理左端点 $a=\alpha$，解在整个 $(\alpha,\beta)$ 上存在唯一。

最大区间可以有限，即使 $f$ 在整个 $\mathbb R^2$ 上光滑：$y'=1+y^2$、$y(0)=0$ 的解为 $y=\tan t$，最大区间是 $(-\pi/2,\pi/2)$，两端爆破。比较定理可从下方压出爆破上界：若 $y(0)=a>0$ 且 $y'\ge y^2$，则 $y(t)\ge a/(1-at)$，故爆破时刻 $T_*\le1/a$。注意反向比较 $y'\le y^2$ 只给出上界，不能推出 $y$ 一定爆破；例如 $y'=y^2e^{-t}$、$y(0)=1$ 的解 $y=e^t$ 在整个 $\mathbb R$ 上存在。
en: Let $f$ be continuous on an open set $D\subset\mathbb R^2$ and locally Lipschitz in $y$, with $(t_0,y_0)\in D$. The Picard–Lindelöf theorem gives a local solution through $(t_0,y_0)$. If two solutions are defined on open intervals $I_1,I_2$ containing $t_0$, uniqueness makes them equal on $I_1\cap I_2$, so they glue into a solution on $I_1\cup I_2$. Taking the union of all such intervals gives the maximal interval of existence $(a,b)$; it contains $t_0$, and the solution on it is uniquely determined by the initial value.

The maximal interval must be open. If $b<+\infty$ and the solution has a finite limit $y_*$ as $t\to b^-$ with $(b,y_*)\in D$, then applying local existence and uniqueness at $(b,y_*)$ extends the solution to the right of $b$, a contradiction. Hence either $b=+\infty$, or $(t,y(t))$ stays in no compact subset of $D$ as $t\to b^-$; the left endpoint $a$ is treated similarly.

This is the blow-up alternative: if $b<+\infty$, then for every compact subset $K\subset D$ there is $t_K<b$ such that $(t,y(t))\notin K$ for all $t_K<t<b$. In particular, if $D=\mathbb R^2$, then necessarily $|y(t)|\to+\infty$; if $D$ has a boundary, then its limit points can only lie on $\partial D$ or at infinity. The solution never stops quietly at a finite value in the interior of $D$.

Example: $y'=y^2$, $y(0)=1$. Separating variables gives $-1/y=t+C$, and the initial value yields $$y(t)=\frac{1}{1-t},\qquad t\in(-\infty,1).$$ As $t\to1^-$, $y\to+\infty$, so the solution cannot be continued past $t=1$; the maximal interval is $(-\infty,1)$. In general, $y(0)=a>0$ gives $y=a/(1-at)$ with blow-up time $T_*=1/a$.

Linear equations have no finite-time blow-up inside the interval where the coefficients are continuous; however, $p,q$ themselves may be unbounded at the endpoints $\alpha,\beta$, so one cannot assert that the solution has a finite limit there. Suppose the maximal right endpoint is $b<\beta$. Since $[t_0,b]\subset(\alpha,\beta)$ is compact, $P=\max_{[t_0,b]}|p|$ and $Q=\max_{[t_0,b]}|q|$ are finite. For $t\in[t_0,b)$, the integral equation and Gronwall give $$|y(t)|\le\bigl(|y_0|+Q(b-t_0)\bigr)e^{P(b-t_0)}.$$ Also $|y'|\le P|y|+Q$ is bounded, so $y$ is uniformly continuous on $[t_0,b)$; the limit $y_*=\lim_{t\to b^-}y(t)$ exists and $(b,y_*)\in(\alpha,\beta)\times\mathbb R^n$. Local existence and uniqueness then continue the solution to the right of $(b,y_*)$, contradicting the maximality of $b$. Hence $b=\beta$; similarly $a=\alpha$, and the solution exists and is unique on all of $(\alpha,\beta)$.

The maximal interval can be finite even when $f$ is smooth on all of $\mathbb R^2$: $y'=1+y^2$, $y(0)=0$ has the solution $y=\tan t$ on $(-\pi/2,\pi/2)$, blowing up at both ends. Comparison with a lower solution produces an upper bound for the blow-up time: if $y(0)=a>0$ and $y'\ge y^2$, then $y(t)\ge a/(1-at)$, so the blow-up time satisfies $T_*\le1/a$. The reverse comparison $y'\le y^2$ gives only an upper bound and does not force blow-up; for instance $y'=y^2e^{-t}$, $y(0)=1$ has the global solution $y=e^t$ on all of $\mathbb R$.

zh: 设 $y,z$ 在 $[x_0,X]$ 上分别满足 $$y'=f(x,y),\qquad z'=g(x,z),$$ 其中 $f,g$ 连续，$g$ 关于第二个变量局部 Lipschitz（常数 $L$），且对所用范围内的 $(x,u)$ 有 $$f(x,u)\le g(x,u),\qquad y(x_0)\le z(x_0).$$ 则 $$y(x)\le z(x)\qquad(x_0\le x\le X).$$ 结论只对前进方向成立；向回走时不等号可能反转。

令 $w=z-y$。由 $y'\le g(x,y)$ 与 Lipschitz 条件，$$\begin{aligned}w'&=g(x,z)-y'\\&\ge g(x,z)-g(x,y)\ge-L|w|.\end{aligned}$$ 若 $w(x_0)\ge0$，假设存在 $x\in[x_0,X]$ 使 $w<0$。取负值集合在 $[x_0,X]$ 中的一个连通分支 $(c,d)$。若 $c=x_0$，则由 $w(x_0)\ge0$ 与负值分支的连续性得 $w(c)=w(x_0)=0$；若 $c>x_0$，由连续性也有 $w(c)=0$。于是 $w(c)=0$，且在 $(c,d)$ 上 $w<0$，故 $w'\ge Lw$。于是 $(e^{-Lx}w)'=e^{-Lx}(w'-Lw)\ge0$，从 $w(c)=0$ 推出在 $(c,d)$ 上 $w\ge0$，与 $w<0$ 矛盾；所以 $w\ge0$。
严格初值情形：若 $y(x_0)<z(x_0)$，则 $w(x_0)>0$。在第一个零点 $x_1$ 之前有 $w>0$，由 $w'\ge-Lw$ 得 $(e^{Lx}w)'\ge0$，故 $$e^{Lx_1}w(x_1)\ge e^{Lx_0}w(x_0)>0,$$ 与 $w(x_1)=0$ 矛盾。因此 $y(x)<z(x)$ 对 $x>x_0$ 成立；两条解曲线不能相交。

微分不等式形式：若 $y$ 只满足 $y'\le g(x,y)$，则称 $y$ 为**下解**（subsolution）；若 $y'\ge g(x,y)$，则称 $y$ 为**上解**（supersolution）。方向至关重要：下解爆破会强迫其上的解也爆破；但一个较大的解（或上解）爆破，不能推出其下方仅满足 $y'\le g(x,y)$ 的下解也爆破。例：$y'=y^2e^{-x}$、$y(0)=1$ 有解 $y=e^x$，它同时是 $g(x,y)=y^2$ 的下解；$z'=z^2$、$z(0)=1$ 的解 $z=1/(1-x)$ 在 $x=1$ 爆破。$y^2e^{-x}\le z^2$，但 $y=e^x$ 整体存在——较大的解爆破，并没有迫使下方这个下解爆破。

爆破估计的标准用法：若 $y(0)=a>0$ 且 $y'\ge y^2$，取 $z'=z^2$、$z(0)=a$，则 $z(x)=a/(1-ax)$，比较得 $y(x)\ge z(x)$ 于 $[0,1/a)$。当 $x\to(1/a)^-$ 时 $z\to+\infty$，故 $y$ 的最大存在区间右端点 $T_*\le1/a$；若 $y$ 能延拓过 $1/a$，连续性将给出有限的 $y(1/a)$，与 $y\ge z\to+\infty$ 矛盾。反向的 $y'\le y^2$ 只给 $y\le z$，不能断言 $y$ 爆破。

适用范围：结论是标量、单向时间、且 $g$ 关于第二变量 Lipschitz 的情形。没有 Lipschitz 条件时比较可能失败：$y'=\sqrt{y}$、$y(0)=0$ 有解 $y=(x/2)^2$（$x\ge0$）与 $z\equiv0$，二者初值相同且 $y>z$（$x>0$）。对系统 $x'=f(t,x)$，逐分量比较需要 $f$ 的拟单调性（cooperative 条件）或向量比较定理，不能把标量结论直接套用。在 Lipschitz 条件下，若 $f=g$ 且初值相同，比较定理退化为唯一性：两条解曲线不能相交。
en: Let $y,z$ satisfy on $[x_0,X]$ $$y'=f(x,y),\qquad z'=g(x,z),$$ where $f,g$ are continuous and $g$ is locally Lipschitz in its second variable (constant $L$), and for all $(x,u)$ in the relevant range $$f(x,u)\le g(x,u),\qquad y(x_0)\le z(x_0).$$ Then $$y(x)\le z(x)\qquad(x_0\le x\le X).$$ The conclusion holds only in the forward direction; going backwards the inequality may reverse.

Let $w=z-y$. From $y'\le g(x,y)$ and the Lipschitz condition, $$\begin{aligned}w'&=g(x,z)-y'\\&\ge g(x,z)-g(x,y)\ge-L|w|.\end{aligned}$$ If $w(x_0)\ge0$, suppose $w<0$ somewhere in $[x_0,X]$. Take a connected component $(c,d)$ of the negative set inside $[x_0,X]$. If $c=x_0$, then $w(x_0)\ge0$ together with continuity of the negative component gives $w(c)=w(x_0)=0$; if $c>x_0$, continuity again gives $w(c)=0$. Thus $w(c)=0$ and $w<0$ on $(c,d)$, so $w'\ge Lw$. Thus $(e^{-Lx}w)'=e^{-Lx}(w'-Lw)\ge0$, and $w(c)=0$ forces $w\ge0$ on $(c,d)$, contradicting $w<0$. Therefore $w\ge0$.

Strict case: if $y(x_0)<z(x_0)$, then $w(x_0)>0$. Before the first zero $x_1$ we have $w>0$, and $w'\ge-Lw$ gives $(e^{Lx}w)'\ge0$, hence $$e^{Lx_1}w(x_1)\ge e^{Lx_0}w(x_0)>0,$$ contradicting $w(x_1)=0$. Therefore $y(x)<z(x)$ for $x>x_0$; the two solution curves never meet.

Differential-inequality form: if $y$ satisfies only $y'\le g(x,y)$, it is called a **subsolution**; if $y'\ge g(x,y)$, it is a **supersolution**. Direction is essential: blow-up of a subsolution forces every solution above it to blow up; but blow-up of a larger solution (or of a supersolution) does not force a subsolution below it, satisfying only $y'\le g(x,y)$, to blow up. Example: $y'=y^2e^{-x}$, $y(0)=1$ has the solution $y=e^x$, which is also a subsolution for $g(x,y)=y^2$; the solution of $z'=z^2$, $z(0)=1$ is $z=1/(1-x)$, which blows up at $x=1$. Here $y^2e^{-x}\le z^2$, yet $y=e^x$ is global: blow-up of the larger solution does not force the subsolution below it to blow up.

Standard blow-up estimate: if $y(0)=a>0$ and $y'\ge y^2$, take $z'=z^2$, $z(0)=a$, so $z(x)=a/(1-ax)$. Comparison gives $y(x)\ge z(x)$ on $[0,1/a)$. As $x\to(1/a)^-$, $z\to+\infty$, so the right endpoint $T_*$ of the maximal interval of $y$ satisfies $T_*\le1/a$; if $y$ could be continued past $1/a$, continuity would give a finite $y(1/a)$, contradicting $y\ge z\to+\infty$. The reverse inequality $y'\le y^2$ gives only $y\le z$ and does not prove blow-up.

Scope: the conclusion is scalar, one-sided in time, and requires $g$ to be Lipschitz in its second variable. Without the Lipschitz condition comparison can fail: $y'=\sqrt{y}$, $y(0)=0$ has the solutions $y=(x/2)^2$ (for $x\ge0$) and $z\equiv0$; they have the same initial value, yet $y>z$ for $x>0$. For systems $x'=f(t,x)$, componentwise comparison requires quasi-monotonicity (cooperative conditions) or a vector comparison theorem; the scalar result cannot be applied directly. Under the Lipschitz condition, if $f=g$ and the initial values agree, comparison reduces to uniqueness: two solution curves cannot cross.

zh: 设 $x^*$ 是 $x'=f(x)$ 的平衡点，$f(x^*)=0$，$f$ 在 $x^*$ 附近局部 Lipschitz，以保证初值问题解的存在唯一。Lyapunov 稳定是指：对任意 $\varepsilon>0$ 存在 $\delta>0$，使 $\|x(0)-x^*\|<\delta$ 时，对一切 $t\ge0$ 都有 $$\|x(t)-x^*\|<\varepsilon$$（并设这些解在 $t\ge0$ 上存在）。量词顺序是 $\forall\varepsilon\,\exists\delta$；$\delta$ 可依赖 $\varepsilon$，但不能依赖具体初值。只要求解「不跑远」，不要求「跑回来」。

若在稳定之外还存在 $\delta_0>0$，使 $\|x(0)-x^*\|<\delta_0$ 时 $$\lim_{t\to\infty}x(t)=x^*,$$ 则称 $x^*$ **渐近稳定**。因此渐近稳定 = 稳定 + 吸引；稳定的 $\delta(\varepsilon)$ 与吸引的 $\delta_0$ 是两个不同的量，只验证收敛不能自动得到渐近稳定。中心 $x'=y,\ y'=-x$ 是稳定但非渐近稳定的典型：$x^2+y^2$ 沿轨线守恒，轨线绕原点转圈而不趋近。

对线性系统 $x'=Ax$，若所有特征值满足 $\operatorname{Re}\lambda_i<0$，则由 Jordan 标准型存在 $C\ge1$、$\mu>0$ 使 $$\|e^{At}\|\le Ce^{-\mu t},\qquad t\ge0.$$ 于是 $$\|x(t)\|\le Ce^{-\mu t}\|x(0)\|.$$ 给定 $\varepsilon$ 取 $\delta=\varepsilon/C$ 得稳定；又 $x(t)\to0$，故零解全局渐近稳定（而且是指数稳定）。

若某个特征值满足 $\operatorname{Re}\lambda>0$，则零解**不稳定**。取该特征值对应的（广义）特征向量方向上的初值 $x(0)=\delta v$（复特征值时取实部）：解中含 $e^{\lambda t}$（或 $t^k e^{\lambda t}$）因子，其模长随 $t$ 增大而无界。因此对任意 $\varepsilon>0$，无论 $\delta$ 多小，总有时刻 $t$ 使 $\|x(t)\|\ge\varepsilon$，稳定性定义被否定。

对非线性系统 $x'=f(x)$，设 $f\in C^1$、$f(x^*)=0$，$J=Df(x^*)$。若 $J$ 是**双曲**的，即所有 $\operatorname{Re}\lambda_i(J)\ne0$，则平衡点的局部稳定性类型与线性化系统相同：所有实部为负 $\Rightarrow$ 局部渐近稳定（指数稳定）；存在正实部 $\Rightarrow$ 不稳定。证明思路是写 $$f(x)=J(x-x^*)+\rho(x-x^*),\qquad \rho(h)=o(\|h\|),$$ 再用常数变易法与 Gronwall 控制非线性余项；正实部情形由不稳定流形定理给出。结论是局部的，且双曲性不可省。
若出现 $\operatorname{Re}\lambda_i=0$（非双曲），线性化不能下结论，也不存在无条件的逆命题。三个非双曲例子：$x'=-x^3$ 的零解渐近稳定（但非指数）；$x'=x^3$ 的零解不稳定；$x'=y,\ y'=-x$ 的零解稳定但非渐近稳定。它们的 $Df(0)$ 都有实部为零的特征值，结论却不同，说明必须借助 Lyapunov 函数或高阶项分析。
en: Let $x^*$ be an equilibrium of $x'=f(x)$, so $f(x^*)=0$, and let $f$ be locally Lipschitz near $x^*$ so that initial value problems have unique solutions. Lyapunov stability means: for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ such that $\|x(0)-x^*\|<\delta$ implies $$\|x(t)-x^*\|<\varepsilon$$ for all $t\ge0$ (with these solutions assumed to exist for $t\ge0$). The quantifier order is $\forall\varepsilon\,\exists\delta$; $\delta$ may depend on $\varepsilon$ but not on the particular initial point. The requirement is only that solutions stay near, not that they return.

If, in addition to stability, there is $\delta_0>0$ such that $\|x(0)-x^*\|<\delta_0$ implies $$\lim_{t\to\infty}x(t)=x^*,$$ then $x^*$ is **asymptotically stable**. Thus asymptotic stability is stability plus attractivity; the stability tolerance $\delta(\varepsilon)$ and the attraction radius $\delta_0$ are different quantities, and convergence alone does not imply asymptotic stability. The center $x'=y,\ y'=-x$ is the standard stable but not asymptotically stable example: $x^2+y^2$ is conserved along orbits, which circle the origin without approaching it.

For the linear system $x'=Ax$, if every eigenvalue satisfies $\operatorname{Re}\lambda_i<0$, the Jordan form gives $C\ge1$ and $\mu>0$ with $$\|e^{At}\|\le Ce^{-\mu t},\qquad t\ge0.$$ Hence $$\|x(t)\|\le Ce^{-\mu t}\|x(0)\|.$$ Given $\varepsilon$, take $\delta=\varepsilon/C$ to get stability; since $x(t)\to0$, the origin is globally asymptotically stable (indeed exponentially stable).

If some eigenvalue satisfies $\operatorname{Re}\lambda>0$, the origin is **unstable**. Take an initial value $x(0)=\delta v$ in the direction of an associated (generalized) eigenvector (take the real part for complex eigenvalues): the solution contains a factor $e^{\lambda t}$ (or $t^k e^{\lambda t}$), whose norm grows without bound as $t$ increases. Therefore, for every $\varepsilon>0$ and every $\delta>0$, some time $t$ has $\|x(t)\|\ge\varepsilon$, which negates the definition of stability.

For the nonlinear system $x'=f(x)$, assume $f\in C^1$, $f(x^*)=0$, and let $J=Df(x^*)$. If $J$ is **hyperbolic**, i.e. $\operatorname{Re}\lambda_i(J)\ne0$ for all $i$, then the local stability type is the same as that of the linearization: all real parts negative implies local asymptotic (indeed exponential) stability; some positive real part implies instability. The proof writes $$f(x)=J(x-x^*)+\rho(x-x^*),\qquad \rho(h)=o(\|h\|),$$ and controls the nonlinear remainder by variation of constants and Gronwall; the positive-real-part case follows from the unstable manifold theorem. The conclusion is local, and hyperbolicity cannot be dropped.

If some $\operatorname{Re}\lambda_i=0$ (non-hyperbolic), linearization is inconclusive, and there is no unconditional converse. Three non-hyperbolic examples: $x'=-x^3$ has an asymptotically stable origin (but not exponentially stable); $x'=x^3$ has an unstable origin; $x'=y,\ y'=-x$ has a stable but not asymptotically stable origin. Their Jacobians $Df(0)$ all have eigenvalues with zero real part, yet the conclusions differ, so Lyapunov functions or higher-order analysis are required.

zh: 考虑自治系统 $x'=f(x)$，$f$ 在原点附近局部 Lipschitz，$f(0)=0$。设 $V$ 在 $B_r=\{\|x\|<r\}$ 上 $C^1$、$V(0)=0$，且 $0<\|x\|<r$ 时 $V(x)>0$，即 $V$ 正定。沿轨线的导数由链式法则给出 $$\dot V(x)=\nabla V(x)\cdot f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\frac{\partial V}{\partial x_i}f_i(x).$$ 沿任一解 $x(t)$ 有 $\frac{d}{dt}V(x(t))=\dot V(x(t))$；计算它只需 $V$ 的梯度和 $f$，不需要解出 $x(t)$。

若 $\dot V(x)\le0$ 在 $B_r$ 中成立（半负定），则原点稳定。给定 $\varepsilon\in(0,r)$，令 $$m=\min_{\|x\|=\varepsilon}V(x)>0;$$ 正定性保证 $m>0$。由 $V(0)=0$ 与连续性，存在 $\delta\in(0,\varepsilon)$ 使 $\|x\|<\delta$ 时 $V(x)<m$。若解从 $\|x(0)\|<\delta$ 出发，只要它还在 $B_\varepsilon$ 内就有 $V(x(t))\le V(x(0))<m$；一旦 $\|x(t)\|=\varepsilon$ 就会 $V\ge m$，矛盾。故对一切 $t\ge0$ 有 $\|x(t)\|<\varepsilon$。

若除原点外 $\dot V(x)<0$（负定），则原点渐近稳定。稳定性由第 2 步。还需收敛：$V(x(t))$ 单调不增且下有界 $0$，故 $V(x(t))\to L\ge0$。若 $L>0$，取 $x(0)$ 足够小使次水平集 $K=\{x:L\le V(x)\le V(x(0))\}$ 含于 $B_r$、紧且离开原点；在 $K$ 上 $\dot V\le-m_0<0$，其中 $m_0=\min_K(-\dot V)>0$。于是 $$V(x(t))\le V(x(0))-m_0t\to-\infty,$$ 矛盾。故 $L=0$，即 $V(x(t))\to0$；由 $V$ 正定与连续性得 $x(t)\to0$。

若 $V$ 正定而 $\dot V$ 正定（除原点外 $\dot V>0$），则原点不稳定。取任意 $\delta>0$，选 $x(0)$ 满足 $0<\|x(0)\|<\delta$ 且 $V(x(0))>0$。沿轨线 $V$ 严格递增，故 $V(x(t))\ge V(x(0))>0$，轨线不能进入原点。若该轨线对所有 $t\ge0$ 都留在某个紧球 $B_\rho$（$0<\rho<r$，这里 $V$ 在 $B_r$ 上有定义）内，则 $V(x(t))$ 有上界且递增，收敛到 $L\ge V(x(0))>0$。取 $\omega$-极限点 $x_*\ne0$，则 $V(x_*)=L$，且 $\omega$-极限集不变；但 $\dot V(x_*)>0$，沿经过 $x_*$ 的轨线 $V$ 严格增加，与 $V$ 在 $\omega$-极限集上为常数矛盾。故该轨线无界，必离开任意给定的球；由 $\delta$ 任意，原点不稳定。

半负定只给稳定；要升级为渐近稳定需要额外条件。LaSalle 不变性原理：若 $V$ 正定、$\dot V\le0$，且 $E=\{x:\dot V(x)=0\}$ 中最大的不变子集就是 $\{0\}$，则原点渐近稳定（在轨线有界或 $V$ 的次水平集紧的条件下）。例：阻尼振子 $$x'=y,\qquad y'=-x-y,\qquad V=\frac12(x^2+y^2).$$ 则 $$\dot V=xy+y(-x-y)=-y^2\le0.$$ $E=\{y=0\}$；在 $y=0$ 上 $y'=-x$，只有 $x=0$ 时才能停留在 $E$ 中，故最大不变子集为原点，原点是渐近稳定的（$V$ 径向无界，事实上全局渐近稳定）。

对线性系统 $x'=Ax$，取 $V=x^{\mathsf T}Px$、$P>0$，则 $$\dot V=x^{\mathsf T}(A^{\mathsf T}P+PA)x=-x^{\mathsf T}Qx,$$ 其中 $Q=-(A^{\mathsf T}P+PA)$。若对某个 $P>0$ 有 $Q>0$，则 $\dot V$ 负定，原点渐近稳定。反过来，$A$ 的所有特征值实部为负，当且仅当对任意 $Q>0$，方程 $A^{\mathsf T}P+PA=-Q$ 都有唯一正定解 $P$。若 $V$ 还径向无界且 $\dot V<0$，则结论升级为全局渐近稳定。注意：Lyapunov 函数不唯一、没有通用构造法；逆定理（在适当光滑性下）只保证存在，不给出公式；不能把「存在某个 $V$」误当成「任意 $V$ 都行」。
en: Consider the autonomous system $x'=f(x)$, where $f$ is locally Lipschitz near the origin and $f(0)=0$. Let $V$ be $C^1$ on $B_r=\{\|x\|<r\}$ with $V(0)=0$ and $V(x)>0$ for $0<\|x\|<r$; that is, $V$ is positive definite. The orbital derivative is given by the chain rule: $$\dot V(x)=\nabla V(x)\cdot f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\frac{\partial V}{\partial x_i}f_i(x).$$ Along any solution $x(t)$, $\frac{d}{dt}V(x(t))=\dot V(x(t))$; computing it requires only the gradient of $V$ and the vector field $f$, never the solution itself.

If $\dot V(x)\le0$ on $B_r$ (negative semidefinite), the origin is stable. Given $\varepsilon\in(0,r)$, set $$m=\min_{\|x\|=\varepsilon}V(x)>0;$$ positive definiteness guarantees $m>0$. By $V(0)=0$ and continuity, there is $\delta\in(0,\varepsilon)$ such that $\|x\|<\delta$ implies $V(x)<m$. If a solution starts with $\|x(0)\|<\delta$, then as long as it remains in $B_\varepsilon$ we have $V(x(t))\le V(x(0))<m$; if $\|x(t)\|=\varepsilon$, then $V\ge m$, a contradiction. Hence $\|x(t)\|<\varepsilon$ for all $t\ge0$.

If $\dot V(x)<0$ for $x\ne0$ (negative definite), the origin is asymptotically stable. Stability comes from Step 2. For convergence, $V(x(t))$ is nonincreasing and bounded below by $0$, so $V(x(t))\to L\ge0$. If $L>0$, choose $x(0)$ small enough that the sublevel set $K=\{x:L\le V(x)\le V(x(0))\}$ lies in $B_r$, is compact, and stays away from the origin; on $K$, $\dot V\le-m_0<0$ with $m_0=\min_K(-\dot V)>0$. Then $$V(x(t))\le V(x(0))-m_0t\to-\infty,$$ a contradiction. Hence $L=0$, so $V(x(t))\to0$; positive definiteness and continuity then give $x(t)\to0$.

If $V$ is positive definite and $\dot V$ is positive definite ($\dot V>0$ for $x\ne0$), the origin is unstable. For any $\delta>0$, choose $x(0)$ with $0<\|x(0)\|<\delta$ and $V(x(0))>0$. Along the trajectory $V$ strictly increases, so $V(x(t))\ge V(x(0))>0$ and the trajectory cannot enter the origin. If this trajectory stayed in some compact ball $B_\rho$ with $0<\rho<r$ (where $V$ is defined on $B_r$) for all $t\ge0$, then $V(x(t))$ would be bounded and increasing, hence converge to $L\ge V(x(0))>0$. Take an $\omega$-limit point $x_*\ne0$; then $V(x_*)=L$, and the $\omega$-limit set is invariant. But $\dot V(x_*)>0$, so $V$ strictly increases along the trajectory through $x_*$, contradicting the fact that $V$ is constant on the $\omega$-limit set. Hence the trajectory is unbounded and must leave every prescribed ball; since $\delta$ was arbitrary, the origin is unstable.

Negative semidefiniteness gives only stability; upgrading to asymptotic stability requires an extra condition. LaSalle's invariance principle: if $V$ is positive definite, $\dot V\le0$, and the largest invariant subset of $E=\{x:\dot V(x)=0\}$ is $\{0\}$, then the origin is asymptotically stable (provided trajectories are bounded or the sublevel sets of $V$ are compact). Example: the damped oscillator $$x'=y,\qquad y'=-x-y,\qquad V=\frac12(x^2+y^2).$$ Then $$\dot V=xy+y(-x-y)=-y^2\le0.$$ Here $E=\{y=0\}$; on $y=0$ we have $y'=-x$, so a trajectory can remain in $E$ only if $x=0$. The largest invariant subset is thus the origin, and the origin is asymptotically stable (since $V$ is radially unbounded, in fact globally so).

For the linear system $x'=Ax$, take $V=x^{\mathsf T}Px$ with $P>0$. Then $$\dot V=x^{\mathsf T}(A^{\mathsf T}P+PA)x=-x^{\mathsf T}Qx,$$ where $Q=-(A^{\mathsf T}P+PA)$. If $Q>0$ for some $P>0$, then $\dot V$ is negative definite and the origin is asymptotically stable. Conversely, every eigenvalue of $A$ has negative real part if and only if, for every $Q>0$, the equation $A^{\mathsf T}P+PA=-Q$ has a unique positive definite solution $P$. If moreover $V$ is radially unbounded and $\dot V<0$, the conclusion upgrades to global asymptotic stability. Caveat: Lyapunov functions are not unique and there is no general construction; the converse theorem (under suitable smoothness) guarantees existence but gives no formula; one must not mistake "there exists some $V$" for "every $V$ works".
